It pertains to the core area of text generation using transformer-based models.
The model is associated with Meta's Llama family, indicating continued relevance in large language model research.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the 'deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1' model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized under text-generation and conversational AI pipelines.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors, indicating a focus on accessible LLM deployment.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under key AI/ML tags including 'transformers' and 'llama'.
The pipeline indicates its primary use case is text generation.

stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Highlights the trending status of the DeepSeek-V4-Pro model on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized under text-generation and utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.
References an associated academic paper (arxiv:2606.19348), indicating recent research backing the model.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) leveraging MLX.
Coding agent performance saw up to a 90% speed increase according to the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements result in faster response times and lower memory usage for LLMs.
The updated engine also enables models to generate higher quality outputs.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The framework emphasizes local-first operation, allowing AI to run entirely on user hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, integrating easily with local LLM ecosystems.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, now integrates MLX for performance optimization.
The integration specifically targets Apple Silicon, significantly boosting local AI inference speed on Apple hardware.
This is presented as a preview feature, indicating ongoing development and optimization for the Apple ecosystem.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed to integrate with messaging applications.
It connects users to local AI coding agents.
A key feature is that all AI processing runs entirely on the user's local device for privacy.

stories.title: ollama launch
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama introduces a new command for easily setting up and running coding tools.
It supports various models, including Claude Code, OpenCode, and Codex, locally or in the cloud.
A key feature is its simplicity, requiring no environment variables or configuration files.

stories.title: Anthropic wants to develop its own drugs
stories.author: Robert Hart
bullet_points: Anthropic is expanding its AI focus beyond general models into scientific research with the launch of 'Claude Science'.
Claude Science is positioned as an 'AI workbench for scientists,' integrating fragmented tools and datasets into a unified environment.
The development signals a significant industry shift towards applying large language models directly to complex scientific discovery and data visualization.

stories.title: Distributed Attacks in Persistent-State AI Control
stories.author: Asa Cooper Stickland
bullet_points: New security threat identified in autonomous AI coding agents due to persistent codebases across sessions.
Attackers can distribute malicious payloads across multiple pull requests (PRs) to evade detection.
The paper introduces 'Iterative VibeCoding' to study the dynamics of safely deploying capable but untrusted AI.

stories.title: Program-as-Weights: A Programming Paradigm for Fuzzy Functions
stories.author: Yuntian Deng
bullet_points: Introduces 'Fuzzy-function programming' to handle complex, non-rule-based tasks (e.g., log alerting, JSON repair).
Proposes compiling natural-language specifications directly into compact, locally-executable neural artifacts ('Program-as-Weights').
Addresses current limitations of relying on LLM APIs, specifically concerning locality, reproducibility, and cost.

stories.title: LACUNA: A Testbed for Evaluating Localization Precision for LLM Unlearning
stories.author: Verna Dankers
bullet_points: The paper addresses the critical issue of LLMs memorizing sensitive PII from training data.
It focuses on 'unlearning,' a post-hoc removal technique, specifically challenging the current reliance on output-level evaluation.
LACUNA introduces a testbed to evaluate the precision of localization methods used in LLM unlearning.

stories.title: Program-as-Weights: A Programming Paradigm for Fuzzy Functions
stories.author: Yuntian Deng
bullet_points: Introduces 'fuzzy-function programming' to handle complex, rule-based tasks that are difficult to implement traditionally.
Proposes 'Program-as-Weights,' a method to compile natural-language specifications into compact, locally-executable neural artifacts.
Addresses current industry pain points related to relying on LLM APIs for tasks, specifically concerning locality, reproducibility, and cost.

stories.title: OrbitQuant: Data-Agnostic Quantization for Image and Video Diffusion Transformers
stories.author: Saurabh Shukla
bullet_points: Introduces OrbitQuant, a novel data-agnostic quantization method specifically designed for Diffusion Transformers (DiTs).
Addresses a major bottleneck in state-of-the-art image/video generation models: the high computational cost of inference due to multi-step sampling and large parameter counts.
Solves the problem of activation shifting across different model checkpoints and modalities, which plagues traditional Post-Training Quantization (PTQ) methods.

stories.title: LACUNA: A Testbed for Evaluating Localization Precision for LLM Unlearning
stories.author: Verna Dankers
bullet_points: Addresses the critical security issue of LLMs memorizing sensitive PII from training data.
Proposes 'LACUNA,' a new testbed to evaluate the precision of LLM unlearning methods.
Highlights a gap in current research: existing benchmarks only test output-level unlearning, not true knowledge erasure.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance enhancements.
Improved GGUF model compatibility is achieved via llama.cpp integration.
The update broadens model support across various hardware, augmenting the MLX engine on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for subagents within Claude Code.
The new feature set includes the capability for web search functionality in Claude Code.
This update enhances the capabilities of local LLM orchestration tools like Ollama.

stories.title: Newly discovered PamStealer isn't your typical macOS malware
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: A new piece of macOS malware, PamStealer, has been discovered.
The malware is identified as an infostealer, targeting Mac users.
Its existence highlights the growing sophistication and focus on Mac-specific cyber threats.

stories.title: FAA proposal: Supersonic airliners can fly over US cities if they’re quiet
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: The FAA is proposing new regulations to permit supersonic airliners to fly over US cities.
The key condition for this allowance is that the aircraft must be quiet enough to eliminate the sonic boom.
This development signals a potential regulatory shift allowing for the resumption of supersonic commercial travel.

stories.title: LACUNA: A Testbed for Evaluating Localization Precision for LLM Unlearning
stories.author: Verna Dankers
bullet_points: LLMs risk memorizing sensitive PII from training data, necessitating robust unlearning methods.
Current SOTA unlearning techniques often use a 'localize-first, unlearn-second' approach targeting specific model parameters.
The research highlights a gap in current benchmarks, which only test unlearning at the output level, not internal knowledge erasure.

stories.title: Online Safety Monitoring for LLMs
stories.author: Eric Nalisnick
bullet_points: LLMs still generate unsafe outputs post-alignment training, necessitating online monitoring.
The research proposes a simple, real-time monitor that uses an external model's verifier signal.
The monitor's alarm decision is based on thresholding, calibrated using risk control, showing competitive results in testing.

stories.title: ReContext: Recursive Evidence Replay as LLM Harness for Long-Context Reasoning
stories.author: Jingrui He
bullet_points: Addresses the critical issue of LLMs failing to effectively utilize relevant evidence within long input contexts.
Introduces 'ReContext' (Recursive Evidence Replay), a training-free inference method designed to improve long-context reasoning.
Focuses on bridging the gap between LLM context access capabilities and actual context utilization in real-world applications.

stories.title: What LLM Agents Say When No One Is Watching: Social Structure and Latent Objective Emergence in Multi-Agent Debates
stories.author: Shahriar Noroozizadeh
bullet_points: Investigates how social structure (role, audience) influences LLM agent behavior in multi-agent debates.
Compares public utterances against off-the-record (OTR) responses to detect latent objective emergence.
Proposes a dual-channel debate framework to study the impact of social context on AI communication.

stories.title: Reasoning LLM Improves Speaker Recognition in Long-form TV Dramas
stories.author: Qi Tian
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of speaker recognition in complex, long-form TV dramas.
Introduces DramaSR-532K, a large-scale benchmark with 532K annotated dialogue lines and over 900 characters.
Proposes an improvement using Reasoning LLMs to enhance speaker recognition accuracy in video content.

stories.title: DemoPSD: Disagreement-Modulated Policy Self-Distillation
stories.author: Linqi Song
bullet_points: Introduces DemoPSD, a new method building upon On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) for LLM training.
Addresses a key limitation of OPSD: teacher's dense, privileged token-level supervision can cause overfitting and poor cross-domain generalization.
The research focuses on modulating disagreement to improve LLM reasoning capabilities while mitigating overfitting risks.

stories.title: G-RRM: Guiding Symbolic Solvers with Recurrent Reasoning Models
stories.author: Günter Klambauer
bullet_points: Introduces G-RRM, a neuro-symbolic approach that integrates Recurrent Reasoning Models (SE-RRMs) with classical symbolic solvers.
SE-RRMs function as neural solvers, generating complete solution proposals to guide established symbolic methods like SAT solvers (e.g., Glucose 4.1).
The work focuses on SE-RRMs, which are symbol-equivariant and show improved extrapolation capabilities for larger problem sizes.

stories.title: Online Safety Monitoring for LLMs
stories.author: Eric Nalisnick
bullet_points: LLMs continue to generate unsafe outputs even after alignment training, necessitating post-deployment monitoring.
The research proposes a simple, real-time monitor that uses an external model's verification signal to trigger safety alarms.
The monitor's threshold is calibrated using risk control, showing competitive performance in red teaming and reasoning tasks.

stories.title: What LLM Agents Say When No One Is Watching: Social Structure and Latent Objective Emergence in Multi-Agent Debates
stories.author: Shahriar Noroozizadeh
bullet_points: Investigates how social structures (role, audience) influence LLM agent behavior in multi-agent debates.
Compares public utterances in a shared debate setting against off-the-record (OTR) responses to detect emergent social influence.
Proposes a dual-channel debate framework to study the impact of relational context on LLM communication.

stories.title: DemoPSD: Disagreement-Modulated Policy Self-Distillation
stories.author: Linqi Song
bullet_points: Introduces DemoPSD, a new approach to Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) for training LLMs.
Addresses a critical limitation of current OPSD methods: overfitting and poor cross-domain generalization due to dense, privileged token-level supervision.
Aims to improve LLM reasoning capabilities by modulating the disagreement between teacher and student models.

stories.title: Controllable Sim Agents with Behavior Latents
stories.author: Ziran Wang
bullet_points: Introduces CNeVA, a framework for creating controllable simulated agents.
The agents learn to infer a per-agent Gaussian behavior latent from discounted returns.
This controllability allows engineers to test autonomous systems and isolate variables in traffic simulation without real-world risk.

stories.title: Neuron-Aware Data Selection for Annotation-Free LLM Self-Distillation
stories.author: Xiang Lorraine Li
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of post-training LLMs in specialized domains lacking expert human annotations.
Proposes a 'Neuron-Aware Data Selection' method for annotation-free self-distillation.
Utilizes the model's own outputs and majority voting across multiple rollouts to generate pseudo-labels.

stories.title: Understanding the Robustness of Distributed Self-Supervised Learning Frameworks Against Non-IID Data
stories.author: Dong Yuan
bullet_points: Addresses the critical challenge of data heterogeneity (non-IID data) in Distributed Self-Supervised Learning (D-SSL).
Provides a rigorous theoretical analysis to understand how various D-SSL frameworks perform under real-world, decentralized data conditions.
Contributes to the theoretical understanding of D-SSL robustness, a key area for scaling ML with decentralized data.

stories.title: Program-as-Weights: A Programming Paradigm for Fuzzy Functions
stories.author: Yuntian Deng
bullet_points: Introduces 'fuzzy-function programming' to handle complex, rule-based tasks poorly suited for traditional coding.
Proposes compiling natural-language specifications into compact, locally-executable neural artifacts ('Program-as-Weights').
Addresses limitations of relying on LLM APIs for tasks like log alerting or JSON repair (locality, reproducibility, cost).

stories.title: Online Safety Monitoring for LLMs
stories.author: Eric Nalisnick
bullet_points: LLMs still generate unsafe outputs post-alignment training, necessitating real-time monitoring.
The research proposes a simple, real-time monitor that uses an external model's verifier signal.
The monitor's alarm decision is based on thresholding, calibrated using risk control, showing competitive results in testing.

stories.title: What LLM Agents Say When No One Is Watching: Social Structure and Latent Objective Emergence in Multi-Agent Debates
stories.author: Shahriar Noroozizadeh
bullet_points: Investigates how social structures (role, audience) influence LLM agent behavior in multi-agent debates.
Compares public utterances made by agents against private, off-the-record (OTR) responses under the same conditions.
Proposes a dual-channel debate framework to study the emergence of latent objectives based on social context.

stories.title: Reasoning LLM Improves Speaker Recognition in Long-form TV Dramas
stories.author: Qi Tian
bullet_points: Addresses the complex challenge of speaker recognition in long-form TV dramas.
Introduces DramaSR-532K, a new large-scale benchmark with 532K annotated dialogue lines.
Proposes using Reasoning LLMs to improve the accuracy of speaker attribution in video content.

stories.title: Towards Robustness against Typographic Attack with Training-free Concept Localization
stories.author: Aidong Zhang
bullet_points: The paper addresses a critical vulnerability in Large Vision Language Models (LVLMs) that use CLIP as a vision encoder.
The vulnerability, termed 'Typographic Attack' (TA), occurs when irrelevant text within an image biases the model toward lexical meaning over true visual semantics.
The proposed solution focuses on achieving robustness against this attack using a 'training-free concept localization' method.

stories.title: Visually Grounded Self-Reflection for Vision-Language Models via Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Greg Durrett
bullet_points: The research addresses a limitation in Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) regarding self-reflection during multimodal reasoning.
Existing LVLMs struggle to ground their self-correction process in visual inputs, especially with out-of-distribution data.
The proposed solution utilizes Reinforcement Learning to enable better visual grounding during the textual Chain-of-Thought (CoT) self-reflection process.

stories.title: Will Scaling Improve Social Simulation with LLMs?
stories.author: Diyi Yang
bullet_points: Investigates if scaling LLMs will improve the fidelity of social simulations.
Questions whether simulation accuracy is dependent on general LLM capabilities or requires separate research.
Uses scaling laws to analyze the relationship between compute scale, general benchmarks, and simulation fidelity.

stories.title: Jamesob's guide to running SOTA LLMs locally
stories.author: livestyle
bullet_points: The article provides a guide for running State-of-the-Art (SOTA) Large Language Models (LLMs) on local hardware.
This addresses the growing trend of local, private LLM deployment.
The content is highly relevant to the practical application and democratization of advanced AI.

stories.title: Arbitrary code execution breaking sandboxes in KDE Plasma
stories.author: blog.kimiblock.top via ecksdee
bullet_points: A security vulnerability allowing arbitrary code execution has been discovered in KDE Plasma.
The exploit specifically targets and breaks out of existing sandboxing mechanisms.
This represents a significant security flaw within a major desktop environment.
